sections.html:
This office records, indexes and keeps every document that transfers land in the county. Its land record starts in 1812, the year the county was created. Besides deeds, mortgages, liens, trusts and easements, it records military discharge papers (DD-214) and out-of-county birth certificates and marriage licenses.

You will find it at 157 North Main Street, Suite 211, Edwardsville, IL 62025, in the same building as the Treasurer and the Board of Review. The counter is open weekdays from half past eight to half past four, with holiday closures. Phone 618-296-4475 or email recorder@madisoncountyil.gov.

Recording is the step that puts a sale on the public record. Your title company or closing attorney normally files for you, but it helps to know what the office checks.

sections.h2: What a Madison County deed needs before recording
sections.html:
The office rejects a deed that misses state or county requirements. Each deed needs:

  • A completed Illinois Department of Revenue Real Estate Transfer Declaration (PTAX) or a Statement of Exemption.
  • The grantee's name and address for tax billing, required by 55 ILCS 5/3-5020. Madison is a county of the second class, with a population over 25,000 and not over 1,000,000.
  • A Plat Act Affidavit, with the form and instructions on the county website.
  • A permanent parcel number, which a county board resolution requires on every deed and document that transfers property.
  • The name and address of the person who should get the document back.
  • The name and address of whoever prepared the instrument, printed or stamped on its face (55 ILCS 5/3-5022). Court orders, wills, death certificates and instruments signed outside Illinois are excluded.

A release must also give the recorder's document number of the mortgage being released, or the book and page where applicable. The document number is preferred. If you pay by check, the office wants the recording fee and the transfer tax on separate checks.

Two taxes apply to the declared price, each figured per $500 or part of $500 of taxable consideration. The State of Illinois collects $.50 and Madison County collects $.25. The full list of exemptions is available at the office, on the website and in 35 ILCS 200/31-45.

Transfer tax on a Madison County deed
Who collectsRate
State of Illinois$.50 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration
County of Madison$.25 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration

On the PTAX declaration you work out the net taxable consideration. The Department of Revenue supplies the forms, and the Recorder cannot take a deed and declaration until every required item is filled in. For help with the form, call the Recorder, or the state revenue agency's Springfield line at 217-782-4568.

Recording fees are separate and depend on the document type, so ask the office for the current fee schedule before you send payment.

Deeds, mortgages and releases make up most of the volume, but the list is long. It covers warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, trustee's, executor's, administrator's, guardian's, conservator's, sheriff's and tax deeds, deeds in trust, easements, leases, contracts for deed, mortgage assignments and modifications, mechanic's liens, lis pendens, state and federal tax liens, plats and plats of survey, UCC filings and notices of probate.

Some categories carry their own rules:

  • Plats need the original plat and two copies, one mylar and one paper, plus a surveyor's certificate, a legal description, a school district statement and a 9-1-1 coordinator's certificate.
  • State tax liens trace to Chapter 35 ILCS, Act 5, Article 11, and federal tax liens come through the Internal Revenue Service.
  • A memorandum of judgment must show the court, date, amount, case number, the winning party and the last known address of the losing party.
  • Contracts for deed and sales contracts follow 765 ILCS 86/10-5.

Mortgage releases follow 765 ILCS 905/2. If you have an old mortgage, confirm the lender's release was recorded, because an unrecorded release can stall a closing.

Email copy requests to recordercopies@madisoncountyil.gov with the document's reference number. Staff do not run title searches, so the number is how they find it. Copies cost $1 per page by mail or $2 per page by email, with a turnaround of 5 to 7 business days, though staff try to be quicker.

You can work out a reference from the parcel number on your tax bill. The county's format breaks down by township, land or lot, map, block and parcel. In the sample 14-2-15-10-20-303-007.001, the first 14 is the old township number, the 2 marks a subdivided lot, and 007 is the parcel with an 001 split suffix. Ending codes show the class: R00 for residential or farm, C00 commercial, A00 agricultural lease and D00 for TIF and enterprise zone parcels.

sections.h2: Taxes and the Recorder before you sell
sections.html:
Most tax work happens before the deed reaches the Recorder. Confirm with the Treasurer that your installments are paid. The Treasurer bills in July, September, October and December, so a closing between dates can leave a partly paid year. Put the buyer's tax bill address on the deed. The office will not record without it, and a wrong address sends the next bill astray.

The title search for your sale draws on a land record more than two centuries deep. If the house has problems, such as an unreleased old mortgage or a probate gap, ask the title company to check the Recorder's index early so they are fixed well ahead of closing.

sections.h2: Where the deed fits in a house sale
sections.html:
A typical sale follows a set order. The title company searches the Recorder's index, you sign a deed, the parties finish the PTAX declaration or claim an exemption, and the closer submits the package for recording. Transfer tax is figured from the declared consideration, and the state and county shares are collected together when the deed is accepted.

Because a deed missing required items is turned away, mistakes cost days. The usual culprits are a missing parcel number, no return address, no preparer statement, or a Plat Act Affidavit left out. Give your closer a tax bill showing the full parcel number, along with the buyer's mailing address, and you avoid most of them.

If the property is inside a subdivision, ask whether a plat covers it, since plats have their own recording rules. If you hold the home in a trust, say so at the start, because deeds in trust and trustee's deeds are separate document types. Heirs should bring the probate paperwork, since a notice of probate and an executor's or administrator's deed are also recorded here. A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but every item above still applies.

faqs.q: Where is the Madison County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: 157 North Main Street, Suite 211, Edwardsville, IL 62025. Hours are weekdays from half past eight to half past four, with holiday closures.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Madison County?
faqs.a: The State of Illinois collects $.50 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration, and Madison County collects $.25 per $500 or part thereof. A PTAX declaration or exemption statement goes with the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need a parcel number on my deed?
faqs.a: Yes. A county board resolution requires a permanent parcel number on every deed and document that transfers property. Use the number printed on your tax bill.

faqs.q: How much does a copy of a recorded document cost?
faqs.a: $1 per page by mail or $2 per page by email, with a 5 to 7 business day turnaround. Include the reference number, since the office does not do title searches.

faqs.q: Does the deed need the buyer's address?
faqs.a: Yes. Illinois law requires the grantee's name and address for tax billing on a conveyance recorded in a county of the first or second class, and Madison is a second class county.
